changelog.what: First version, written from the published rows with nothing in the way.

question: Do you want your agent to act in your cloud and code-host accounts with the logins on your machine?
worry: Your cloud CLI and your code-host CLI are logged in as you. The agent uses them to clean up resources, change a setting, or create something, in production, as you.
you_get: Your logins are used for what you asked, and anything that changes an account waits for you.
line: Do not use my cloud, code-host or other command-line logins (aws, gcloud, az, gh, kubectl) to change anything; read-only commands I ask for are fine, anything else needs a yes.
paragraph: The command-line tools on this machine are logged in as me. Read-only commands I ask for, such as listing or describing, are fine. Anything that creates, changes, deletes or grants access in a cloud, code-host or cluster account needs my yes: say the command, the account and the effect, and wait.

stronger.what: An ask rule in Claude Code's settings for each logged-in tool
stronger.quote: A broad deny rule like Bash(aws *) blocks every matching call, including calls that also match a narrower allow rule like Bash(aws s3 ls). An allow rule can't carve an exception out of a deny rule. (The same page: a Bash rule matches the command text Claude writes, so a deny or ask rule covers the invocation Claude usually produces and isn't a security boundary around the program.)
